title: Causal rebase operation journal
description: Private supervised-replay and recovery journal, stored worktree-private at .git/vcs-lab/rebase.json while a causal rebase is in progress (src/rebase-operations.js startOperation). v2 carries the whole rewrite program rather than only the replay queue, so a merge-preserving operation can rebuild its parent mapping after an interruption (ADR-0034). v3 adds the declared interactive program of ADR-0035 — `reword`, `edit`, `squash`, and `fixup` as plan actions, each with its own identity rule — and is a strict superset of v2.

state.description: 'prepared', 'reducing-overlay', 'resetting', 'running', 'positioning', 'applying', 'conflicted', 'blocked', 'forecast-mismatch', or 'identity-mismatch'. 'reducing-overlay' is the moment before the reset onto the new base when the worktree is being returned to the committed head, with the overlay already safe in its checkpoint (ADR-0028). 'positioning' is a merge-preserving operation moving to the parent its next step applies onto (ADR-0034). 'awaiting-message' and 'awaiting-content' are the two interactive pauses: a `reword` waiting for its new message, and an `edit` waiting for the caller to change content (ADR-0035). Both come after the change is applied, so the work is already in the worktree when the caller is asked.

predictedOverlayTree.description: The worktree tree the forecast predicted after the overlay is put back, verified after the committed result verifies and before anything is published. Null, or absent, when no overlay is in play (ADR-0028).

targetOverlay.description: The overlay this rebase carries: uncommitted work the caller captured in a checkpoint, reduced away before the picks and re-materialized onto the rewritten tip afterwards (ADR-0028). The overlaid worktree is the source branch's own, because a rebase rewrites the branch the caller is standing on. Recorded in the journal so an abort can put the captured worktree back, and so a resumed operation in a new process knows an overlay is in play. Null, or absent, when there is none.

draftChangeId.description: Display and audit only. It is not a plan entry, not a coverage input, and not a receipt subject: a receipt claims nothing about an uncommitted state.

rematerialized.description: Always 'uncommitted': the overlay never enters committed history through this path.

overlayRematerialized.description: True once this operation has put the overlay back into the worktree, which happens after the committed result verifies and before the re-materialized tree is compared with the prediction. Journaled because it is what tells an abort that a dirty worktree in 'forecast-mismatch' is this operation's own doing rather than the user's, so the recovery ADR-0028 names stays reachable. Absent or false otherwise.

queue.description: Every step of the rewrite, in the order it runs. A `pick` replays one change; a `recreate-merge` joins two mapped parents; an `omit` runs nothing and exists only so a later merge naming that commit as a parent resolves to whatever replaced the commit beneath it. A linear operation is all picks.

executedCount.description: Steps that ran, which is the cursor into the forecast's steps. It differs from `nextIndex` exactly when the program carries an `omit`, because a forecast has no entry for a commit nothing replayed.

rewritten.description: Original commit to the commit that replaced it, so an interrupted merge-preserving operation can resume with the same parent mapping. Each entry is also named by a ref under refs/vcs-lab/rebase/<operation id>/, which the operation releases when it finalizes or aborts.

recreatedMerges.description: The joins recreated so far. They are not applications and never become ones (ADR-0034).

commit.description: The subject the action applies to.

target.description: For `squash` and `fixup`, the commit that survives and keeps its identity; null for `reword` and `edit`, which name only a subject.
